- Because the stack is vitest + typescript, "testable" here means: the AC can be expressed as

- Stories in scope are transit-fare and departure-board behavior (e.g. fare charged for a rider

  appear in the listed output, is specific; an AC saying "fares are correct" is not.
- Boundary conditions are the recurring risk in this domain. For age/threshold and
  first/last-element stories, the edge cases that matter are the values immediately at and
  either side of the boundary. If the ACs pin the success path but never state what happens at
  the boundary itself, that is the classic "enrichable" shape here.
- Both tickets in scope are defect reports, not feature requests. Treat them as symptom
  descriptions and apply the enrichment rule below with full force.

CLASSIFICATION RULES:
- "sufficient": ACs are present, specific, testable, and cover the primary success path
  AND at least one error/edge case. Agent can implement without asking questions.
- "enrichable": ACs exist but are vague, incomplete, or missing error paths. Agent can
  expand them using the description and standard engineering judgment. Low risk of drift.
- "insufficient": ACs are absent, entirely non-testable ("user can do X"), or so ambiguous
  that different engineers would implement fundamentally different things. Human must clarify.

A story whose expected behavior cannot be located anywhere in mocka at all — no such surface
exists in the codebase — is still judged on its ACs, not on whether the code exists. Absence of
the surface is an investigation finding for a downstream step, not an AC verdict. Do not
downgrade a well-specified story because you suspect the feature is unimplemented.

ENRICHMENT RULE (critical): enrichedAcs must describe OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR to VERIFY — never HOW to implement it. Do NOT prescribe an internal mechanism or algorithm. Forbidden: "calculate independently", "split", "halve"/"×0.5", "per segment", "for each line item", adding new fields/flags, or any phrasing that presumes a particular code approach. A bug ticket describes a SYMPTOM ("the amount is not displayed for the return leg"); keep the enriched ACs at that symptom/behavior level (what a tester observes), and enrich ONLY for clarity, testability, and genuinely-missing edge/error cases. Inventing an implementation approach in an AC misdirects the downstream code investigation toward the wrong fix.

PROJECT-SPECIFIC ENRICHMENT TRAPS: in this codebase the tempting-but-forbidden phrasings are
comparison-operator and index arithmetic. Never write an enriched AC that says which operator to
use, that a bound is inclusive or exclusive "in the comparison", that an off-by-one exists, that
a loop or slice range should change, or that a particular function should be modified. Name no
file, function, or variable in an enriched AC. Say what a tester sees for a stated input — "a
rider aged 65 is charged the senior fare", "the board lists the final stop of the route" — and
add the neighbouring boundary inputs as their own observable ACs so the downstream investigator
is free to find the real cause.
